# Joint Statistical Meetings 2026

I had the opportunity to present my research at the **2026 Joint Statistical Meetings (JSM)** in Boston, Massachusetts.

This conference brought together statisticians from academia, industry, and government to discuss recent advances in statistics and biostatistics.

![](jsm-sign.jpg)

## Poster Presentation

I presented the poster

> **Adaptive Weighting for Time-to-Event Continual Reassessment Method:
> Improving Safety in Phase I Dose-Finding Trials**

The work introduces an adaptive predictive weighting approach that reduces
overdosing while maintaining accurate maximum tolerated dose (MTD)
selection.

### Key Findings

- 40.6% reduction in overdosing
- Maintained MTD selection accuracy
- Drop-in replacement for the standard TITE-CRM
- Applicable to Phase I oncology trials

![](jsm-poster.jpg)

Standing beside my poster during the JSM poster session.

## Research Impact

This work addresses one of the major challenges in Phase I oncology trials:
delayed toxicity.

Instead of relying on fixed linear follow-up weights, the proposed method
uses adaptive predictive weights based on observed toxicity timing,
improving patient safety while preserving trial efficiency.

The manuscript is currently under review at
*Statistics in Medicine*.
